en: So how can you access locally running large
language models programmatically with help
of LM Studio?
Well, as a first step in LM Studio, you
should go to power user or developer since
now it is all about development.
And then there to this developer view, this
developer area here.
And there you must switch this status of the
LM Studio LM Studio server, which is the
thing you will be able to access
programmatically, from stopped
to running.
As a result of doing that, you'll get a log
output down there which shows you log
messages from requests that were sent to
that server.
You can clear that and you'll see any new
messages
as they arrive or as new requests hit the
server.
You see the API endpoints, so the URLs you
could say, to which you can send requests
to,
for example,
get a list of available models or to
generate a new response from a model.
And you see the domain to which you have to
send these requests. So you send them to a
combination of that domain and then this
endpoint.
Now, if you don't know anything about
writing code, then
this lecture and this part of this section
won't be for you because, of course,
programmatically using large language models
only is interesting if you know how to write
code or if you at least have a basic
understanding of how programming works.
Of course, you can use a large language
model to generate code for you, but you
still need to have a general understanding
of what an API is and what it means to send
a request to an API.
But if you got that, then LM Studio has you
covered because now we got a running server
running locally on our system, only
accessible by us here on our machine. So not
available to the World Wide Web unless you
configured your machine to be reachable from
everyone else out there, of course, which by
default won't be the case.
And you then also get some settings you can
tweak here. About that server. Now, for
example, the port,
which is also reflected here, to which the
requests have to be sent.
You can configure just-in-time model
loading, which means
if a request would be sent for a model
that's not currently loaded in LM Studio, it
would then be loaded on demand.
You can turn this off if you don't want
this, but if you turn it on, the advantage
is that you don't have to load models in
advance. Of course, requests for models that
aren't loaded yet will take a bit longer
because the model has to be loaded first.
And you can also control that a model should
be auto-unloaded if it hasn't been used for
a while, for 60 minutes, for example, as a
default.
So these are some settings you can tweak,
but with that, the server is up and running.

how can you use that server?
